307	/-- The adaptation's equations are regular: at `z ∈ D(h_j)` the pointwise clause
308	`eqn_rel j z` presents the germ of `f_j` as a unit germ times the germ of `d`'s regular

310	theorem eqn_regular (j : A.index) (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ A.pieces j) :

/-!
# Zariski-local certification of a seed system: relaxing the global certificate gate

The DD-R endgame consumes divisor families through `DivFamZar` (`DivisorFamilyZar.lean`),
whose membership predicate is `IsLocallyCertified`: some span-`⊤` family `g : Fin m → R`

certificate over `R` itself.**

is exactly the hypothesis that is FALSE for arbitrary extracted pieces (I-0209: a piece
whose support trace leaks has a non-finite colength, and the localization repair breaks
finiteness over `R`).  The lane has been paying for a strictly stronger statement than
its consumer needs.

This file lands the relaxation.  `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` says: to
certify a system *Zariski-locally* it suffices to produce, for each member of some

pulled system.  Then `ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_away_isCertified`

/-!
# No-leak over a shrunken base, with no fibre hypothesis

The certificate assemblers consume, per piece `j`, the fibrewise clause

`∀ s, (fibre over s) ∩ closure (supp ∩ pieces j) ⊆ pieces j`

(`isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`), equivalently emptiness of the **leak locus**
`supportLeak (pieces j) = closure (supp ∩ pieces j) \ pieces j`
(`Scheme.LocalEquations.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`).

The `tube-fibre` leaf of the DD-R lane tried to obtain this by putting the whole support
inside a single piece.  That shape is refuted — `DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean`,
`not_exists_unique_support_piece`: both pinned charts carry a partition of unity, so a
support point of `V₀ ⊓ V₁` always lies in two distinct pieces.

This file gets the clause a different way, and **without any fibre analysis**.  The leak
locus is closed, and under a universally closed structure morphism its base image is closed
too (`isClosed_image_supportLeak`).  So:

* over the *open complement* of that base image, nothing leaks;
* that complement is a Zariski neighbourhood of every base point it contains, refinable to a
  basic open — the `Localization.Away` shape the pointwise gate consumes.

The leak locus is a genuine obstruction only over its own base image, which is a **closed**
subset of `Spec R`. So the no-leak clause is available on a Zariski-dense open of the base
for free; what a fibre analysis is still needed for is the base points *inside* that closed
image.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_basicOpen_supportLeak_eq_empty` — a basic
  open around any base point outside the leak's image, over which nothing leaks.
* `Scheme.LocalEquations.forall_fibre_closure_subset_of_supportLeak_inter_eq_empty` —
  leak-freeness over an open of the base gives the assembler's fibrewise clause there.
-/

/-!
# No-leak over a shrunken base, with no fibre hypothesis

The certificate assemblers consume, per piece `j`, the fibrewise clause

`∀ s, (fibre over s) ∩ closure (supp ∩ pieces j) ⊆ pieces j`

(`isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`), equivalently emptiness of the **leak locus**
`supportLeak (pieces j) = closure (supp ∩ pieces j) \ pieces j`
(`Scheme.LocalEquations.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`).

The `tube-fibre` leaf of the DD-R lane tried to obtain this by putting the whole support
inside a single piece.  That shape is refuted — `DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean`,
`not_exists_unique_support_piece`: both pinned charts carry a partition of unity, so a
support point of `V₀ ⊓ V₁` always lies in two distinct pieces.

This file gets the clause a different way, and **without any fibre analysis**.  The leak
locus is closed, and under a universally closed structure morphism its base image is closed
too (`isClosed_image_supportLeak`).  So:

* over the *open complement* of that base image, nothing leaks;
* that complement is a Zariski neighbourhood of every base point it contains, refinable to a
  basic open — the `Localization.Away` shape the pointwise gate consumes.

The leak locus is a genuine obstruction only over its own base image, which is a **closed**
subset of `Spec R`. So the no-leak clause is available on a Zariski-dense open of the base
for free; what a fibre analysis is still needed for is the base points *inside* that closed
image.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_basicOpen_supportLeak_eq_empty` — a basic
  open around any base point outside the leak's image, over which nothing leaks.
* `Scheme.LocalEquations.forall_fibre_closure_subset_of_supportLeak_inter_eq_empty` —
  leak-freeness over an open of the base gives the assembler's fibrewise clause there.
-/

/-!
# The support tube in `Away`-chart form

The pointwise certificate gate (`DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean`) asks, at each base prime
`p`, for an element `r ∉ p` such that the pulled system is certified over
`Localization.Away r`.  The support tube (`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube`)
delivers piece isolation over an *abstract* Zariski neighbourhood `V` of `p`.  This file
refines that neighbourhood to a basic open — the shape `Localization.Away` needs — and
records the resulting statement.

The refinement is the standard fact that basic opens form a topological basis of
`Spec R` (`PrimeSpectrum.isBasis_basic_opens`); the content is only that the tube's
conclusion is monotone in the neighbourhood, so shrinking `V` to a basic open inside it
preserves support isolation.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_basicOpen_supportTube` — the tube with a
  basic-open neighbourhood: an `r ∉ p` whose basic open isolates the support inside `U`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_notMem_supportLocus_subset_of_fibre` — the same for the
  relative curve over a test ring, with the properness licence supplied.
-/

set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

namespace Scheme.LocalEquations

variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (d : X.LocalEquations)

/-- **The support tube with a basic-open neighbourhood.** If the support fibre over a base
prime `p` lies inside an open `U`, then some `r ∉ p` has its whole basic-open preimage's
support inside `U`.

The tube produces an abstract neighbourhood; basic opens are a basis of `Spec R`
(`PrimeSpectrum.isBasis_basic_opens`), so shrinking to a basic open inside it keeps the
conclusion by monotonicity of the preimage. This is the form the `Localization.Away`
charts of `IsLocallyCertified` consume. -/
theorem exists_basicOpen_supportTube (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))
    [UniversallyClosed f] {U : Set X} (hU : IsOpen U) {p : PrimeSpectrum R}
    (hfib : f.base ⁻¹' {(p : Spec (CommRingCat.of R))} ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U) :
    ∃ r : R, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
      f.base ⁻¹' (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen r : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))
        ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U := by
  obtain ⟨V, hpV, hV⟩ := d.exists_supportTube f hU hfib
  -- refine `V` to a basic open around `p`
  obtain ⟨W, hWmem, hpW, hWV⟩ :=
    PrimeSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_basic_opens.exists_subset_of_mem_open
      (a := p) hpV V.isOpen
  obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := hWmem
  exact ⟨r, (PrimeSpectrum.mem_basicOpen r p).mp hpW,
    fun x hx => hV ⟨hWV hx.1, hx.2⟩⟩

# The certificate of a support-separated adaptation

The DD-R certificate lane was built around the equalizer `W(d) = ker (δ_left − δ_right)`
of the two overlap-restriction arrows.  Its two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4), and the
kernel-spanning input of `isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`, are the genuinely hard

adaptation over the shrunken base, we are free to choose one whose pieces are
**support-separated**: each off-diagonal overlap misses the divisor, so its overlap
colength vanishes.  For such an adaptation

* `δ_left = δ_right` on the nose (`deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated`), hence

* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_separated` — the certificate from

-/

variable [IsFinite π] {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)

/-- **The (c1)-finite clause from a closed support trace** (the core adaptation
corollary): if the piece trace of the family support is closed in the relative curve,
the chart-local colength `Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)` is a finite `R`-module — the
`IsCertified.finite_colength` clause at `j`, and the `[Module.Finite]` input of the
landed `projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField`.  Consumes the properness
licence (`instIsProperRelCurveHom`); no Noetherian hypothesis. -/
theorem finite_colength_of_isClosed_supportLocus_inter (j : A.index)
    (hclosed : IsClosed (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))) :
    Module.Finite R (A.colength j) := by
  rw [A.supportLocus_inter_pieces j] at hclosed
  exact (A.toFinCoverData.isAffineOpen_pieces j).finite_quotient_span_singleton_of_isClosed
    (A.eqn j) hclosed

/-- The (c1)-finite clause in the leak-locus spelling: nothing leaks out of the piece
`j`, so the trace is closed and the colength is finite. -/
theorem finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty (j : A.index)
    (hleak : d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅) :
    Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
  A.finite_colength_of_isClosed_supportLocus_inter j
    ((d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (A.pieces j)).mpr hleak)

/-- **The (c1)-finite clause from fibrewise no-leak data** (the CertUniv threading
slot): if over every base point the fibre of the closure of the piece trace stays in
the piece — the topological shadow of the P-fib-N fibrewise finiteness data combined
with the seed design — then the colength of the piece `j` is a finite `R`-module. -/
theorem finite_colength_of_forall_fibre_closure_subset (j : A.index)
    (hfib : ∀ s : Spec (CommRingCat.of R),
      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))
        ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
    Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
  A.finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty j
    (d.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_forall_fibre
      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) hfib)

/-- The (c1)-finite clause when the piece dominates the support: if the whole family
support lies in the piece `j` (the shape the support tube produces after shrinking the
base), the colength is finite.  The fibrewise form `∀ s, fibre ∩ supportLocus ⊆ piece`
reduces to this hypothesis by `fun x hx => hfib _ ⟨rfl, hx⟩`. -/
theorem finite_colength_of_supportLocus_subset (j : A.index)
    (hsub : d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
    Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
  A.finite_colength_of_isClosed_supportLocus_inter j (by
    rw [Set.inter_eq_left.mpr hsub]
    exact d.isClosed_supportLocus)

end DivisorAdaptation

end Adaptation

81	/-! ## The module-theoretic core -/
82	
83	/-- **Base change of a module along a field extension preserves triviality**: for an
84	`S`-module `H` and a field extension `L → L'` inside the `S`-tower, `H ⊗[S] L` is
85	subsingleton iff `H ⊗[S] L'` is.
86	
87	Going up is `0 ⊗ = 0`; coming down is the faithful flatness of the (nonzero) field
88	extension `L → L'` (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_reflects_triviality`), read across the
89	base-change-in-stages equivalence `(TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange)`.
90	**Separability is not used** — every field extension is faithfully flat. -/
91	theorem subsingleton_tensorProduct_field_ext_iff
92	    {S L L' H : Type u} [CommRing S] [Field L] [Field L'] [Algebra S L] [Algebra S L']
93	    [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower S L L'] [AddCommGroup H] [Module S H] :
94	    Subsingleton (H ⊗[S] L) ↔ Subsingleton (H ⊗[S] L') := by
95	  have e := TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange S L L' L' H
96	  rw [(TensorProduct.comm S H L).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr,
97	      (TensorProduct.comm S H L').toEquiv.subsingleton_congr,
98	      ← e.toEquiv.subsingleton_congr]
99	  exact ⟨fun _ => inferInstance,
100	    fun _ => Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_reflects_triviality L L' (L ⊗[S] H)⟩
101

108	/-! ## The witness predicate as a function of the fibre field -/
109	
110	/-- **The chart-membership witness predicate at a field `L`** — the field-parametrised
111	form of the set of `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing`
112	(`Pic0ChartLocusOpen`): the fibre class of `D` at `L` admits an effective witness divisor
113	with vanishing `H¹`.  For `L = q.asIdeal.ResidueField` this is definitionally membership
114	of `q` in the keystone-1 witness locus. -/
115	def BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
116	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L] [IsScalarTower k B L] : Prop :=
117	  ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
118	    Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W
119	        = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B L) D.cechPicClass
120	      ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)
121	
122	/-- The witness predicate is the engine's complex-form fibre condition
123	`Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] L)`, via the two-way datum dictionary
124	`subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (C1, GAP-6). -/
125	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_subsingleton
126	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L]
127	    [IsScalarTower k B L] :
128	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L ↔ Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] L) :=
129	  (D.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness L).symm
130	
131	/-! ## The fibre-field invariance (the gap-2 core) -/
132	
133	/-- **CHART-U(b) gap-2 core — fibre-field invariance of witness h¹-vanishing**: for a
134	pinned datum `D` over the affine base `B` and a field extension `L → L'` inside the
135	`k`/`B` tower (the residue-field seam `κ(p) → κ(q)` of a carrier map `comap f`), the
136	witness h¹-vanishing of `D` at `L` transfers to and from `L'`.
137	
138	Both sides are, via the datum dictionary, `Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] ·)`, and
139	that transfers along the (faithfully flat) field extension `L → L'`
140	(`subsingleton_tensorProduct_field_ext_iff`).  In particular this covers the separable
141	residue-field extensions of an étale/étale-plus carrier map. -/
142	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
143	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
144	    (L L' : Type u) [Field L] [Field L'] [Algebra k L] [Algebra k L']
145	    [Algebra B L] [Algebra B L'] [IsScalarTower k B L] [IsScalarTower k B L']
146	    [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower B L L'] :
147	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L' := by
148	  rw [D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_subsingleton L,
149	      D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_subsingleton L']
150	  exact subsingleton_tensorProduct_field_ext_iff
151	
152	/-- **The separable specialisation the CHART-U(b) transport (ii) names** (I-0252 gap 2):
153	for a **separable** residue-field extension `L → L'` (`Algebra.IsSeparable`, the case of
154	an étale/étale-plus carrier map), witness h¹-vanishing of `D` transfers between `L` and
155	`L'`.  Separability is recorded to name the intended consumer; the transfer holds for any
156	field extension (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`). -/
157	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable
158	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
159	    (L L' : Type u) [Field L] [Field L'] [Algebra k L] [Algebra k L']
160	    [Algebra B L] [Algebra B L'] [IsScalarTower k B L] [IsScalarTower k B L']
161	    [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower B L L'] [Algebra.IsSeparable L L'] :
162	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L' :=
163	  D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension L L'
164	
165	/-! ## Fixed-field class-intrinsicity (the other half the `comap` identity needs) -/
166	
167	/-- **Class-intrinsicity of the witness predicate at a fixed field** (V1a): the witness
168	h¹-vanishing predicate depends only on the mapped fibre class
169	`Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B L) D.cechPicClass`, so two data — over possibly
170	different bases `B`, `B'` — whose fibre classes at `L` agree have the same witness
171	predicate at `L`.
172	
173	Together with `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` (the `κ(p) → κ(q)` transfer)
174	this is exactly what the CHART-U(b) `comap`-preimage identity reduces to at C9-time; the
175	one residual input is the shifted-datum class identity of I-0252 gap 1 (the Σ/θ
176	naturality), which is divRep-gated. -/
177	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq
178	    {B' : Type u} [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B']
179	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (D' : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B' π)
180	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L] [Algebra B' L]
181	    [IsScalarTower k B L] [IsScalarTower k B' L]
182	    (hcl : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B L) D.cechPicClass
183	        = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B' L) D'.cechPicClass) :
184	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L ↔ D'.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L := by
185	  simp only [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing, hcl]
